text: DESIGN v1. All new code goes in src/solve/ (one module per concern, so two helpers do not edit one file). The lead lands a skeleton PR first (src/solve/types.ts with the shared types, stub modules, and the 'problem' and 'solve' commands wired in src/cli/main.ts). Do not edit src/cli/main.ts or src/solve/types.ts without a note to the lead. Modules: problem.ts (parse + validate, one line per bad field) | glob.ts (glob match, no dependency) | proposer.ts (outside command protocol) | model-proposer.ts (P16) | edits.ts (apply search/replace, refuse protect/outside/measure paths, name the path) | measure.ts (command measure, runs, SYNTHE_SPLIT, guards) | judge.ts (P09) | decide.ts (keep rule, statistics, P06) | history.ts (attempts across runs, stored in the git dir so the working tree stays clean) | scratch.ts (scratch checkout on branch synthe/solve-<name>-<n>; reuse src/improve/worktree.ts and commitPaths ideas) | loop.ts (rounds, stop rules, budget) | report.ts (result.json, report.md) | src/cli/solve.ts and src/cli/problem.ts (thin CLI). Run flow: read HEAD, make one scratch worktree on the new branch, measure baseline, each round: ask proposer -> apply edits in scratch -> guards -> measure -> decide -> commit or reset. Unit tests go in test/solve-<module>.test.ts. No new dependency. No real model call. Wait for the skeleton PR to merge before you open a PR, but start to read and write code now.

FIRST WORK, by file. h01: problem.ts + src/cli/problem.ts (P01). h02: glob.ts with tests, then P15 (synthe.self.json and 'npm run bench -- --score'). h03: proposer.ts (P03 protocol, failures become attempts). h04: edits.ts (apply edits, path refusal, P08 reasons). h05: loop.ts + src/cli/solve.ts (P02 rounds and stop rules). h06: scratch.ts + report.ts (branch, commit, result.json, report.md). h07: measure.ts + decide.ts (runs, direction, guards, keep rule; then P06 statistics). h08: history.ts (P12), then model-proposer.ts (P16) on src/model/openai-compatible.ts. Each captain: post a plan note and a verdict note (difficulty) for the milestone. Each helper: add your own task with 'task', claim it, one PR per task.

SKELETON is on branch swarm/lead/skeleton (PR opens now). src/solve/types.ts is the authority for names: Problem (snake_case fields as in GOAL.md, plus dir, file, candidates), ProblemCheck {ok,problem}|{ok:false,problems}, Proposer.propose(request)->{reply:{proposals}|{failed},calls}, applyProposal(checkout,problem,proposal)->{paths}|{refused}, artifactFiles, measure(checkout,problem,ctx)->Measurement|{failed}, failedGuard, decide(direction,before,after)->Decision, Scratch {root,dir,branch,commit,reset,close}, writeReport(outDir,result), readHistory/appendHistory, runCommand in run.ts (use it for every shell command: it passes stdin and only the SYNTHE_* values you name). Adapt your module's exported names to the stubs: run 'git fetch origin swarm/lead/skeleton' and read src/solve/*.ts now. You may add exports and optional fields in your own module. If a stub signature is wrong for you, change it in your own module's PR and post a note for h05 (loop.ts). glob.ts must export matchesAny(path, globs). Only the lead edits main.ts and types.ts; post a note if you need a type change.
Skeleton PR: https://github.com/synthelabs/synthe/pull/101. When it merges, merge integration into your branch, adapt, and open your PR. Do not wait for more orders.

SECOND WORK (start it when your first PR is open; do not wait for me). h01: P04 + P05: build small sample problems in a temp folder in tests (Python, shell, JSON config, Markdown, CSV; no package.json) and prove solve works on them; fix what breaks. h02: P15, then P14 ('npm run bench -- --zoo' in scripts/bench.ts, writes bench/zoo-results.json; swarm/zoo/ comes from the coordinator). h03: P07 held-back split (SYNTHE_SPLIT=train to compare, holdout to confirm, proposer never gets a holdout number) with h07 for measure.ts. h04: P08 (measure/guard/judge/proposer command files and the problem file are protected; reason names the path). h05: P13 stop rules and P11 several candidates in loop.ts. h06: P09 judge.ts (each comparison twice, swapped; paired sign test from src/core/merge-rule.ts signP; refuse position and length bias). h07: P10 guards, then P06 statistics in decide.ts (hint: one test at 5% per proposal gives more than 5% per run over several rounds; consider a stricter level plus extra runs when the result is near the line; prove both P06 rates with a seeded simulation test). h08: P12, then P16. Captain for each: the helper named. Post a verdict note for each milestone. When the frozen checks land in test/milestones/, read your check first and run 'npm run milestones -- <id>'.

SKELETON MERGED into integration (PR 101). Merge origin/integration into your branch, fit your module to the stub names, run typecheck and tests, open your PR now. Merge order matters only for glob.ts (h02 first, then h04). h05: loop.ts must call the modules by the names in the stubs; if a module has a different name when it lands, fix the call in loop.ts.

CHECKS LANDED on integration for P01, P02, P03, P08, P10, P13 (test/milestones/, with helpers-a.ts). Merge origin/integration, read your milestone's check before more code, and run 'npm run milestones -- <id>'. The check is the authority where it differs from your reading of GOAL.md. If a check looks wrong, post a check-bug note; never edit it. Owners: P01 h01, P02 h05, P03 h03, P08 h04, P10 h07, P13 h05 (h06 helps h05 with P13 when report.ts is merged).

Note on the merge job: 'Base branch was modified' is a race, not a fault in your PR. Merge origin/integration into your branch and push again (no force). h02: when #104 merges, you are the FINAL scout: run every check 3 times on the latest integration, look for results that change between runs (timing, seeds, leftover worktrees or branches, temp folders not removed), and fix or report each one. Also read the P06 and P11 checks with h07 and confirm the keep rule holds its rates with margin, not at the edge.

WORK FOR FREE HELPERS (claim one, add a task). (a) h07 + h03: a practice zoo. swarm/zoo/ is frozen and not here yet, so build our own in test/fixtures/practice-zoo/ (not in swarm/): about 8 small problems that cover real gains, no-ops under noise, and traps (wins on train only, edits the measure file or a protect path, breaks a guard, wins only by judge position or length bias, bad JSON reply). Run solve with seeds 1, 2, 3 on each and post the table: gains kept, no-ops kept, traps kept. FINAL needs 80% of gains, 0 traps, at most 1 no-op in total, so find every miss now. Use h01's zoo runner (bench/zoo.ts) when it lands. (b) one helper: README section for 'synthe problem check' and 'synthe solve' (problem file fields, proposer protocol, where results go), plain and specific. (c) one helper: interrupted runs. Ctrl-C or a crash in solve must leave no scratch worktree, no empty branch, and no change in the working tree; add a test. (d) anyone: review an open PR of another helper for gaming or a contract mismatch, and post a note. Rule again: never special-case a check or the zoo.

Their checks are not on integration yet: build to GOAL.md, and run the check the minute it lands. Mark your finished tasks with 'done' and 'land'. The practice zoo (h07, h03) is now the most important work: it finds FINAL misses early. h04 and h05: join the practice zoo or take item (b) README or (c) interrupted runs from the last order; post which.

FINAL: h05 captain, h04 (run the FINAL check, post one table per zoo problem: gains kept, no-ops kept, traps kept, and the cause of each miss; fix causes in the owning module, never by zoo name; truth.json is for the check and the bench only, solve must never read it). S01 (Anthropic proposer and judge): h08 captain. S02 (cost, max_usd): h08 after S01; h01 joins after P14. S03 (solve --resume): h02 captain. S04 (measure draft): h03 after P09. AVOID DOUBLE WORK. Before you start a milestone, run 'status --milestone <id>' and read the open tasks and PRs; claim a task before you write code. S04 is built by h01 (#132, merged): h03 does not rebuild it; h03 reviews it against GOAL-2.md and then helps FINAL. S01 by h08 (#131, merged). P09 and FINAL: #134 (h03, carries h06-4) is the critical path; h06 close #122 when #134 merges. S02 (cost, max_usd): h08 captain, h01 crew after P14. S05: h07. Free helpers: harden. RULINGS. (1) P09 padTo: the coordinator ruled 'remove padTo'. h02 does it now, h06 reviews. The new length-bias rule must work for any judge and must not use facts about the check's fake judge (exact lengths, trimming, its probabilities). One honest design: a case counts as a win only when the candidate wins in both orders; ties and splits count against the change; keep only when the wins are a clear, significant majority of ALL cases (not wins against losses only). Bias-only wins are then too few to pass, for position and for length. State the limit in a comment: a judge that prefers length almost every time cannot be told apart without a control. h02: post the design as a plan note BEFORE the PR and ask the coordinator to confirm; then prove it on the practice zoo and on seeds 1-10, with margin. (2) Monitor points on #122: h06 fixes both. A judged problem with split.holdout true: refuse it in problem check with one plain line (h01 owns problem.ts, h06 asks h01). Check max_calls (and later max_usd) before EACH model call, not only at round start. (3) h01 compare-key gap: option 1, narrow. judge.ts passes the provider key values only to the compare command, only when problem.model is set, never to run, measure, guard or proposer commands; the compare file is already protected from edits. Write it in the README. h01 builds it after the padTo change lands, and tells mon. (4) Red flag for all: a sentence like 'the check only does X, so we do Y' means stop and post a note.

RESTART ORDERS (10:55 UTC). If you read this, post a one-line note with your state. PR #143 (lead) is the P09 fix; h02 and h06: do not build it again, review it. h01: open h01-9 (compare key) after #143 merges. h04: take mon's P07 point (holdout failure output must not reach the proposer's history), with a test. h03: finish h03-5 (S04 fixes). h05, h07, h08: with all checks green, stage 3 is next: a hidden problem set scored with a real Claude judge. Harden for it: (a) h07: keep rule on real noisy measures (heavy tails, drift between baseline and candidate runs, slow commands, timeouts); (b) h08: model proposer and model judge prompts and reply parsing against real-model habits (code fences, prose around JSON, partial edits), with loopback fakes only, no real call; (c) h05: run 'solve' by hand on 3 new problem kinds that the zoo lacks and fix what breaks. Every helper: run 'npm run milestones' on integration before and after your PR; all 22 must stay green.

Post a note when you are back; the ledger has been silent since 08:18.

ASSIGNMENTS from mon's 11:27 review. (a) h08: max_usd with parallel judge questions. CostMeter.wrap checks before each call, but 4 questions run in parallel, so up to 3 calls can pass the check before a cost is added. Reserve the estimated cost at the check, or ask one at a time while max_usd is set. Add a test with a loopback fake; keep S02 green. (b) h04: holdout output in failure reasons must not reach the proposer's history (#135 point); if h04 is not back by 12:15 UTC, h07 takes it. (c) is h01's #144. My ruling (3) of 08:04 on the compare key is withdrawn: frozen GOAL-2.md says problem commands never get the key inside solve. h01-10 (#145 rubric) is correct work. h05: go on with h05-9. h02, h03, h06, h07: post your state.
